payload.rationale: This sprint retro directly touches three load-bearing areas: (1) the product thesis narratives — AntiSlackPositioning, DecisionsEvaporate, DecisionCaptureAtConsensus, and ZeroEffortCapture — because Tanya's claim that the widget shipped and proved the thesis extends or re-confirms those frames; (2) the Sprint 4 positions — Sprint4ThesisProven, ZephyrIntegrationUnlock, ContextPreservationNextSprint — which are the exact positions this retro could update, extend, or contradict (especially since the existing Zephyr position attributes the unlock to Tina, while this document attributes it more generally); (3) adjacent positions on pricing, architecture, category, and target market that the retro's velocity and delivery claims could bear on. I expanded all four narratives and their child positions because the document's themes (async decision widget, Zephyr integration, velocity metrics) span across them, and missing any would risk a duplicate mint. I did not expand the Documents door further or the Unplaced door since the perspective showed no unplaced positions and the two source documents were already surfaced via the focus section.
